title: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

sense.text:
“For all the gods of the nations are idols”: that is the Lord’s message to us. All of the gods of the other nations, their idols and all of their customs, are idolatry, and that is what so-called Christmas is, and what Thanksgiving is. They have nothing to do with the Bible at all. How in the world are you going to talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land? What kind of thanks is that? It is total evil and lies on the Bible, and the message is sent to warn us to stay away from these hella days, as we call them.

Before we went into captivity we went astray and were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. We are not to keep Christmas, Thanksgiving or so-called New Year’s; all of these are pagan, evil holidays. We are to come together on the Lord’s high holy day, the Sabbath, along with the other high holy days we are to keep.

“But the Lord made the heavens.” Our God, the Most High, made the heavens. It is said that way because our God made everything, and that is the God we are connected with. The nations are dismayed at the signs of heaven; our power is the Most High who made them.

precepts.why:
“He sheweth his word unto Jacob”: so we don’t have idols to deal with, we have the Bible. “His statutes and his judgments unto Israel”: these are our customs, this is who we are. The statutes and judgments were given to the Israelites, and that is what we are supposed to be involved in: God’s word, not idolatry.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”: God has not dealt with any other nation concerning this holy Bible, these holy words. He gave that only to Israel. “And as for his judgments, they have not known them”: his judgments, his statutes and his blessings the nations have not known, because they are not the Israelites.

So the gods of the nations are idols, and the nations have their customs; Israel was given the word of the God who made the heavens. Our customs are his statutes and judgments.

That is why it says the same thing in Jeremiah 10. “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”: he is not speaking to everybody, he is speaking to the house of Israel, the Israelites. This Bible is the book of our fathers; it is literally our book, and new brothers and sisters have to get acclimated to it. We are not supposed to be keeping these wicked holidays. The Most High is against that.

“Learn not the way of the heathen”: learn not the way of the nations, because the nations’ gods are idols, as the Psalm says. “And be not dismayed at the signs of heaven”: don’t be dismayed and wowed by what is going on in the heavens, people talking about astrology and all that. A lot of people are tied up in witchcraft and voodoo. The nations deal with that foolishness, and all of it is idolatry. The Israelites are a special people unto him, set above the nations, and they are not supposed to be dealing with what the nations deal with. We fell up underneath these people because we broke the laws of our father and did not serve him with joyfulness and gladness for the abundance of all things he gave us, so he caused us to serve our enemies. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

“For the heathen are dismayed at them”: that is their problem, not ours. Our power is the Most High; that is why the Psalm says “But the Lord made the heavens.” So who are you to be underneath them, when you are the jewels of God? You men and you women are the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”: the customs of the nations have no validity with the Most High; vain means void of anything credible. Then listen to the custom itself: “for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. They deck it with silver and with gold.” A workman goes into the forest, chops down a tree, brings it out, and they put silver and gold on it. That was recorded in Jeremiah during the Babylonian Empire. After Babylon came Persia and Media, then Greece, then Rome, nearly four empires, and Jesus was born in the time of Rome. So how could Jesus be connected to a so-called Christmas tree brought up from Babylon? What do light bulbs, tin and silver, a tree and a tree stand have to do with Christ? Nothing. That is idolatry.

Our people are tied up in it because they obey Babylonian philosophy and don’t care about the Bible. Many know these scriptures and know Christ has nothing to do with that wicked holiday, but they don’t want to stand up for truth, just as they talk about Jesus Christ as a white man when no scripture in any Bible says that; the Bible records him with woolly hair and skin like burnt brass.

What that hella day really is: Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun. It was sun worship, celebrated on December 25th, Dies Natalis Solis Invicti. Sol means sun and Invictus unconquerable, and it was the commemoration of Nimrod, or Tammuz, whom the women were weeping for in Ezekiel; the yule log represents him. The emperor Aurelian revived the cult and promoted Sol Invictus as the chief god of the Roman Empire, and the Greeks had him as Helios, wearing a sun crown and driving a horse-drawn chariot through the sky: Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer with the sled. That is what the hell people are celebrating. Anybody who keeps celebrating that madness now that they know better is going to be judged by the Most High.

sense.text:
Marriage is the crown, the epitome of civilization. If marriage is not done right, nothing goes well after it: from a man and a woman come children, and children branch all the way down to the population of the whole earth. In the beginning the Lord set up man and woman under his laws, but Satan came to Eve, she beguiled her husband, and Adam left God’s laws and ate sin. The Lord checked Adam, because it was Adam’s job to rule that house. We will never get back to the civility the Bible speaks of until we get marriage down pat. The nucleus of all greatness is the family, which is why the leaders in the beginning said, Where are your wives? If you cannot get your house in order, you cannot rule and cannot be a leader in the camp.

To get to the beauty of civility we must examine the root cause of our downfall into immorality: Satan’s device to keep us destroyed. We obeyed sin rather than the duty of man. “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter”: this is what men are supposed to do. The Most High is calling men to get themselves and their houses in order, to be pillars in their houses, leaders, men of integrity, honesty and valor.

“Fear God”: that is the first thing a man must do. If you fear God, if you fear breaking his commandments, you are not going to go off, and you won’t let something lead you into foolishness, because you know there is a judgment for it. “And keep his commandments.”

“For this is the whole duty of man”: for means because. This is the whole reason God put man on the earth. That is the definition of a man: one that keeps God’s commandments, period, no more, no less. We are a product of God; he fashioned us to operate a particular way, and when he called us to operate that way, the name man was on us. Operate outside of that and you can’t be called a man anymore. That is why our enemies called us boy in slavery and would not give us the title of a man: we truly lost what it is to be a man. Society has redefined men, but according to God a man keeps God’s commandments.

We forgot our duty. Man was put on this earth to rule it with God’s commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering. The earth was made to receive your direction, men, and your women were made to receive your direction: she is called woman because she is of man. When you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction, because you are not connected to her. She is supposed to revolve around you. Sisters, you will never be right if your man is off; you go nowhere without your nucleus, and if you orbit around something else your mind will be out of sync, which is exactly where we are now.

“For God shall bring every work into judgment”: for means because. Keeping his commandments is the whole reason man is here, and it is also because God shall bring every work into judgment. If we are not dealing with our marriages properly, there is going to be a judgment for that, and we are looking at it. Many are trying to figure out what the problem in the black community is: the marriages are messed up. Whoring, adultery, fornication. Ugly means sin, and a little leaven will destroy the whole congregation; it has to be rooted out like a cancer.

“With every secret thing”: the nasty stuff people do behind closed doors, thinking nobody sees. The Lord is going to bring it all out, and he brings it out at the worst time for you. You think years have gone by and you are unscathed; then you sit in the interview for the job and they pull records you didn’t know existed: Is this you? Get out of my office. That is how the Lord is. His eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun.

So as men we must make sure our slates are clean. There is temptation, but we have to be disciplined men: I may not always be motivated, but I am always disciplined. Motivation comes and goes; discipline holds. If sin comes before me, or I am bordering on sin, it stops right there. That is integrity: a spirit connected to righteousness that questions itself, Why am I thinking like this? I am supposed to be a man of God, a representative of the heavenly father.

“Whether it be good, or whether it be evil”: it is all going to come out. So what manner of persons ought we to be, as responsible representatives of God redeemed by his son Jesus the Christ? Men of holiness, integrity, righteousness, dignity, honor and valor.

We grew up in a lawless society. The fathers were stripped from the homes; they let the woman get pregnant but would not let the man raise his sons. In slavery a man was made to lay with his friend’s wife or be castrated, because they wanted his seed, a strong black buck, but would not let him raise it. Now we are no good to our own nation, and men look to men of another nation to solve our problems: Hey, Mr. White Man, come fix my problems. What the hell is that? Men solve problems. All of that happened when the institution of marriage was destroyed.

precepts.why:
The earth itself needs us to bring forth God’s commandments in it. “For the earnest expectation of the creature”: expectation means I am expecting something, and earnest means I am expecting it with a begging kind of attitude. “Waiteth for the manifestation”: manifestation means growth. It is time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men. The earth is waiting for us to get ourselves together.

“Of the sons of God”: the earth is waiting for us men to manifest into gods, to rule this planet properly. Righteous women are waiting for that too. Women cry, Where are our black men? because the father figure in the house was destroyed, and many are orbiting out in society untethered to men. You are supposed to be guiding her, not her guiding you. All of this fell apart from the very beginning, when a woman out of order with her husband brought something from Satan and gave it to Adam.

The woman is like the earth. You plant your seed in her as seeds are planted in the earth to bring forth fruit, and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. Your seed was implanted in her, and from her came the people. So to fulfil the duty of manhood a man must be married: no children, no line and no nation without a wife. Sisters are extremely important, but their minds have to be right.

That is the whole duty of man in Ecclesiastes: the earth, and the woman, are waiting on men who keep God’s commandments.

The Lord even says he will use a bird to bring it out. “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber”: people speak against the council and the leadership and think they are going to get away with it. The Most High says no. Some people have evil thoughts against the leaders; rise before the hoary head.

The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The objective is a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to the counsel and got herself together. But if we cannot give a good account we still have to give one, with grief: they didn’t take the counsel, we tried this, we tried that. We are held responsible, and the account is given to the Most High, the Father.

“For a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter”: the Most High will cause that bird. It may not be a literal bird flying around, but people who took every precaution still get found out, because God brings every secret thing into judgment. The matter will be told on you in your evil. In the judgments people ask, How did he find out? It was that damn bird.

sense.text:
Here the Lord describes Babylon the Great as a woman whose nakedness is to be revealed, showing the ugliness of this country. America robbed and raped the original inhabitants and enslaved us, and she cannot hide it. Yet she gets on the world stage and tries to tell other countries how to be righteous, with her so-called Christian missionaries and morality. This chapter prophesies about this country.

“Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon”: America portrays herself as a virgin, a beacon of righteousness. That is what Lady Liberty is about. That is why Malcolm X and Dr. Martin Luther King were killed: they were about to take to the United Nations how black people were mistreated in the south, and expose the demons of this country on the world stage. She told the nations she was a virgin, but as Revelation says, she committed fornication with many nations. She laid down with all the nations, they are drunk with her words, and her influence is on all of them. She has her backside blown out by all of the damn nations; she is no dainty woman.

“Sit on the ground: there is no throne”: you are not a kingdom; sit down, because you are about to be judged, and you are not going to rule anymore. “O daughter of the Chaldeans”: America is an extension of the Babylonians in how they operate. Although America comes out of Rome, she gets her customs, like Christmas, from actual Babylon. “For thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.”

“Uncover thy locks”: uncover your head, as if you were some righteous woman with her head covered. The Lord says you are not righteous; take that covering off. In the company of a whole lot of men: sit down. Where is your father? Where is your husband?

“Make bare the leg”: like a woman walking down the street trying to get cars to stop, raising the leg. The leg is the lower part, from the knee down. “Uncover the thigh”: now roll the dress all the way up. “Pass over the rivers”: a woman crossing a river lifts her dress so it doesn’t get wet, and when it is lifted all the way you can see her behind, and you can tell whether she is a virgin or has been banged many times.

“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”: she is not a righteous woman, and the Most High says so. That is Babylon the Great. She is not dainty, she is not Lady Liberty; for all she portrays, her nakedness will be seen. This is the same nation that did evil to us while trying to look righteous.

Adam fell weak, and then he blamed the woman. “And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and I am looking for you now. What is going on?

“I was afraid”: Adam was afraid because he knew he had messed up. “Because I was naked”: naked to sin. They were not running around naked; they were now exposed to sin. They were not supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in there. Satan showed it to Eve first.

“Who told thee that thou wast naked?” Who told you, Adam, that you were in sin? “Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?” Now the reckoning comes, and it always happens that way. You are in the group of sin until the day of reckoning; then you are exposed and you look for an excuse to cover your blunder. Adam came out of the trance.

“The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” He pointed his finger at her: it is your fault. But it was not her fault; God put him over her. Sisters hearing this may squirm and think it is about them, but the reason they are out of order is that we men are out of order.

Adam did not have to listen to Eve. Sometimes wives come up with foolishness, and you can deal with it and shut it down, or obey it and end up in a mess. You are the ruler of your house and you know why things are lined up as they are. You take the money from a vital bill to please her, the bill comes, you are in the street, and you say, It was that woman you gave me. She will curse you out: you weren’t supposed to listen to me.

“What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me”: she blamed Satan. Pointing fingers. But from that point Adam lost, and we caught hell. The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and the righteous relationship between the black man and the black woman was destroyed: once each other’s roles are violated, they operate against each other instead of for each other. Then the children come, and where one believes and the other does not, the child is unclean, and comes out with self-esteem issues and all kinds of problems. That destruction mutated down through the generations, from Adam and Eve to our mothers and fathers and to us. For the men, we must restore the order to bring back our civility.

Satan attacked the black family structure, because to destroy a people you must destroy the family, and that is what was done to us in slavery. Satan here is the white man, Esau, the physical counterpart of the spiritual demon Satan. Willie Lynch’s breaking process of the African woman, the women of the twelve tribes of Israel, did to us the same evil Satan did to Eve: it destroyed the marriage. They broke her so she would not revolve around her husband, setting up headquarters in her head so that she revolves around them even while she lies beside her husband at night. She was the most important factor for good economics: broken, she trains her children to submit to labor, and today the children are funnelled into a school-to-prison pipeline. This happened to us because we broke God’s laws, and we have to stand up out of the vomit and pull ourselves out.

So Satan uses our women to keep the man subdued; she is his greatest resource. She is like your field: you plant your seed in her, and you must protect that field, because an enemy wants to sow his seeds in your field and take it from you. A man will kill to protect that woman, because his whole nation depends on the union between him and her. As men we are to be gods and judges over this earth, but Satan uses his number one weapon, our women, to bind us. He approaches her because she is the weaker vessel, just as he approached Eve to deceive Adam. So make sure it is your words going into her, not the nations’. Brothers who are proving, prove these women right: put your foot down in wisdom, place a hedge around her, and don’t be distracted by her beauty.

precepts.why:
Satan showed sin to Eve first; Luke shows what Satan does. “And Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost returned from Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what you brothers are going to go through: you are going to be tempted. But men are supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, and that is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

“If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread”: you’ve got the power, why are you sitting here hungry? Satan was trying to get Christ to forget why he was fasting, like a man fasting with a cupboard full of food who goes and eats and loses his purpose and the course he was on. That is what happens with women: they will forget the course they are on. That is why men have to protect her; she is in serious trouble without a husband.

“It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Christ threw it back at him: we live by the word of God, which is why I am fasting, so don’t tempt me with food.

“And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time”: Satan took it up a level. This is what Satan did to Eve. The Bible is abridged; he hit her several times, she resisted, so he took her up and showed her something greater: you don’t have to be under your husband, there will come a time when you will be over him. He showed her America: this man serving you, selling drugs for you, committing crimes for you, worshipping you. She was tired of him telling her to cook and to do this and that, and in the back of her mind she could not stand him, because that vision was there. She went back to Adam, put her beauty on him, didn’t tell him about the death, tantalized him, and got him to bite.

“All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them”: you won’t have to listen to him anymore. That is exactly what is going on in many marriages now: the man can’t tell the woman a damn thing. “For that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it”: whoever will listen to me, I will give that power. He gave Eve that power and that thought. So the beginning was spiritual fornication: she fornicated with Satan in spirit and brought it back to Adam, like a damn threesome. That is why Adam was naked.

sense.text:
Beauty is deceitful, and brothers have to be on their game. Judith was on a righteous cause for her people, and her objective was to get Holofernes’ head cut off, which is a beautiful thing. But this shows the power of beauty and how it can deceive.

“Her sandals ravished his eyes”: we have never seen Judith, but reading it, men imagine how the sandals and the feet looked. It tore him up. “Her beauty took his mind prisoner”: her beauty captivated his brain. “And the fauchion passed through his neck”: a fauchion is a broad, single-edged sword, wider near the point, like a heavy cleaver or machete. Like a sickle, it took his head. She was able to cut his head off because he was so blinded and captivated by her beauty.

Many men have gone out of their wits for women, because that is the power women have over you when you are weak. Women are beautiful and men love nothing better, but you can’t let that deceive you. Judith ravished his eyes and never laid with him; she did just enough to win victory for her people.

She had been mourning the death of her husband, and she took off her mourning garments and put on her beauty for that occasion, to ravish his mind and eyes and get her chance to cut off his head. She knew the power of beauty in righteousness. Sisters, you can do that for your husband, and you will be surprised at the motivation that comes out of a brother who feels he has somebody in his corner. Some brothers work double shifts because they don’t want to go home.

This is a heavy scripture. “Favour is deceitful”: sisters’ profiles with the hair done, holding up a plate of food. That is favor. A hungry brother who never had a woman cook for him, tired of beans and canned goods, can smell it through the screen. But it is deceitful: she put all that on the plate, but did she do anything with her spirit? If you are not looking at the spirit behind it, you are going to get hoodwinked.

“And beauty is vain”: it will fade. “But a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised”: that is what you are supposed to look for. We want the beauty and the plate of food; we love beautiful women. Sisters, your job is to please him and fix yourself up, and when he is happy he will open the wallet. But beyond that, give me the righteousness, a woman that fears God. Then I don’t have to worry; I have no need of spoil; I can trust her. And if she proved you right, she knows you won’t take advantage of her.

Then you can have children on that foundation, and the child will be in love with mom and dad. That is the beginning of a whole new society of righteousness, of civility. We have to start it now, before the Lord gives us the kingdom: who will commit to your trust the true riches if you have not learned to deal righteously while you are here?

Turmoil in the house comes because people did not properly prove each other, and did not look for the righteous example the Bible says a woman should be and a man should be. It goes both ways: a sister too quick to give herself is ruined a few years later, left with a baby or two by a man who is gone.

Favor is deceitful and beauty is vain, and used the wrong way, you will find that this woman is worse than death. They say, She has the body of a devil and the face of a saint; listen to the satanic message behind that. Beauty can be that deceitful, and it will be used to destroy you brothers if you are not on your game: keeping the commandments of God and pressing toward the kingdom.

“And I find more bitter than death the woman”: what could be worse than death? This type of woman is, and some brothers are living in this very verse. “Whose heart is snares and nets”: her mind is thinking of ways to trap you and keep you from doing the work of God. Put God second and put me first, because Satan told her to tell you that. You don’t see the Edomite woman doing that to the Edomite man. Sisters, if the shoe doesn’t fit, don’t wear it; take the notes, and when you find sisters who operate this way, put this on them: if our man isn’t right, we won’t be right.

The house has to be taken care of, but a man has the Lord’s business to handle, and she should not get in his way. If her mind is according to his mind, it should not even come up; she understands that he is handling the Lord’s business, and when he comes back he will handle her. People rush through things to get to the body, ignore the signs, and then, like Adam, say it was that woman you gave me, or it was leadership’s fault.

“And her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”: if you want to please God, you have to escape this type of woman, even though she has that plate of food. This is not for after you are married; it is for while you are proving, before you are betrothed. If you cannot get it straightened out in sincerity, escape from it, because it will bring complete hell on you.

A woman will give a man her body, put herself in the most vulnerable position to receive a baby or a disease, but will not listen to what a righteous man says; nobody taught her the value of her body. She will submit to her boss and to Esau’s system, but not to you. Satan has her mind and you have her body, and when she gets up she goes right back to her father, her true husband, the devil, because that is who she listens to. Some rushed the proving process to reach the year mark leadership gave; but a year was only a benchmark, not a biblical deadline, and people hold secrets for years.

We have bastardized the sanctity of marriage and don’t understand how special it is. At a wedding, with the brother and the sister standing there, this is the day the Lord has made: at that moment they have the opportunity to produce gods, to produce righteousness on this earth and change the world. That is done with God’s blessing because it was done the right way, proved the right way, and the Lord blesses them as he blessed Tobias and Sarah, who prayed together. That is what you want.

“But the sinner shall be taken by her”: the simpleton who looks only at her body, at her sandals, and ignores the spirit behind her, is taken by her beauty, her deception, her plate of food and her nice words. Reports keep rolling in of adultery and fornication, and if men and leaders don’t address it, the problems manifest. The best way is to deal with it at its inception, in the proving process: check every box, confer with your leadership, your fathers and your mothers. We are not trying to do this twice; we want to grow old together. Picture her with gray hair; beauty fades, and if it was all superficial you are left with a person you can’t stand, and children by her.

This is not making it gender specific: it was Eve who went to Adam because Satan went to Eve, and all kinds of evil is projected at our women to keep you brothers subdued. You can’t rule if your house is messed up, and then we never get out of this captivity. Adam had it made; he was entering immortality, and there was no immorality, only civility, but because he didn’t check Eve he lost it and hell followed. Marriage is supposed to be paradise, not a prison, not a ball and chain; she is his help meet. No matter how powerful your new phone is, if the charging station at home is not charging it, it is nothing: when you come home your wife is supposed to charge you up, so you can go out and win again, and you build her up too. Her beauty is meant to help him win wars, not to deceive him. A man not operating the way God made him is defiled too.

This is what happened to us when we fell and lost paradise. “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”: this city is the kingdom. We want to get back to the kingdom, and when we get there we want you women to come with us.

“The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”: danger on both sides. Now we walk a thin line with fire on one side and deep water on the other: trials. One of them is dealing with our women and these marriages, getting our children, our houses and our lives in order. Adam had to work by the sweat of his brow; we have to go through hell to get back, and if we don’t do it, it won’t get done.

“And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once”: we cannot escape the judgments we have to go through. You have to go through it yourself; I can’t pull you through and you can’t pull me. We can give counsel all around, but everybody goes through his own trial.

“If this city now were given unto a man for an inheritance, if he never shall pass the danger set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?” How shall we get the kingdom if we don’t go through the fire? It takes work and discipline. Don’t be tempted with this and that; stay in the commandments. The minute you see anything causing you to bend these laws, stop, because that is exactly how we got into this mess: we started bending the laws a little because it was tempting and tantalizing.
“Even so also is Israel’s portion”: all the Israelites have to go through this.

“Because for their sakes I made the world”: if the whole planet was made for the Israelites’ sake, then God put it in the spirit of the world to want us to rule it. The earth is yearning for you to deal with it, and the woman, made for you, is yearning in her spirit for you to be men again. There is a righteousness deep down in her, but you are going to have to work to get to it. “And when Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done”: when Adam messed up, then came hell, then came prison.

“Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail: they are but few and evil, full of perils”, and “very painful.” “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit”: in the beginning, before this happened, it was wide. The kingdom was ours: civility, beauty, all of it, no death. We had it made.

“If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up”: if we don’t go through these trials, doing things the proper way, we can never get to the kingdom. We messed up, there is a consequence for it, and we have to fix it to get back what we lost, and then some.

“One that ruleth well his own house”: this is how leaders have to be, and leaders means men, period. People try to escape the role by saying, I’m not a bishop, I’m not a deacon, I’m just a regular man. If you are a man, you are made to lead. How can people cut out parts of this and say it is not talking about them? What are you, a homo? A man is supposed to want to fulfil everything a real man does: rule, in righteousness of course, but rule.

“Having his children in subjection with all gravity”: you have to be over your household, brothers, and allow no disrespect or disobedience in keeping God’s commandments. Don’t let anyone, family members or anybody else, come inside your home and defile your house and your family. That is why the man is the one coming to the door with the tool: you have to protect what is behind you. All men are charged with this.

“For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” If you can’t rule your own house, you can’t rule anything. You can’t deal with the church of God, and you won’t be in the kingdom. Wimps and men who don’t want to do what the Most High instructs men to do are not going to be in the kingdom; that is all going to be burnt up. The only men in the kingdom will be real men who stand up for God’s commandments, so we had better get used to it now.

This is the kind of men we have to aspire to be. “These are they which were not defiled with women”: defiled means sullied, marred or spoiled; impaired, debased, degraded, corrupted, tainted, tarnished, ruined. It is not just a word for women; men are defiled when they are not operating the way God made them. Defiled with women means not only women but philosophies and other things: nothing is supposed to take you off the purpose for which God made you, and once you operate outside of it, you are defiled, damaged. These men will stand up for righteousness and will not be deterred. Watch yourself, replay your own actions in your mind, and catch yourself before you wreck yourself.

“For they are virgins”: not necessarily virgins physically, but virgins in this truth. They have put off the weak nature, the sins and the cares of the world: those who came in and repented. It can also speak of the five wise and five foolish virgins, but here it is on this level.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men”: redeemed from the filth. You were in the filth, in the vomit, at a serious deficit, and you had to be brought up. “Being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb”: we have been cleaned up for the Lord, men and women, and we have the chance to get it right.

“And in their mouth was found no guile”: no lies in their mouths, so you don’t have to worry about a bird flying around delivering anything. “For they are without fault before the throne of God”: that can only be when you are keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Christ.

precepts.why:
That is what virgins means: “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

There is such a thing as history, but your history only comes up if you keep doing what you used to do; then it becomes a blot on your record today. So whatever you sisters went through, don’t worry about it; clean yourselves up while you are here, and the same for you brothers. None of us was born in this truth, and we all have a chance to get ourselves correct.

None of this teaching is to condemn anyone. It comes from concern for our people. Leaders have to see the reports, and even a few incidents are enough; one is too many. The question will be asked up there what happened to so-and-so, and the leaders want to be able to give an answer. All things are become new: that is what Revelation is talking about.

“For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband”: the Most High sent his son Christ, and that is where the espousal is made, because Christ died for us, his woman. We are men physically, but we are his bride, which is why the term is used. He cleaned us up and sanctified us through his truth, and once he cleaned us up, we became virgins with him. Old things are passed away.

“That I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ”: that is crystal clear, and it is what Revelation means by they are virgins. Once our slate is cleaned, we are not dirtying it up, not defiling it, not messing it up.

sense.text:
A husband needs a wife as a helper and a stay: stability. If he has a wife who is not spiritually mature and stable, his own stability as a man will be weak in times of trouble. Her mind has to be right so she can be a proper aid to the husband who wants to do the right thing. And she must be teachable: even with her mind right, there will be moments when you have to teach her, and she has to be willing to sit down and listen to you, her husband, not the captains. She has to be teachable so you can put wisdom into her mind, until her mind fully becomes your mind. That is why she is called woman: she is of man.

“The beauty of a woman cheereth the countenance”: men come home from war, from all kinds of crap out there, and the woman builds him up, so he is ready to go to war again and take care of her. A woman who tears him down makes him not even want to go home. His countenance needs cheering because he caught hell out there, and her beauty does it, physical and spiritual.

Beauty goes much further than what you see. A woman on a show was asked where she wanted a man to take her on a date, and she said, You make that decision, I’m here to follow you. When she spoke all the other women faded to black, because her spirit was so different from theirs; the brother could not even get his words out.

“And a man loveth nothing better”: he wants that because he needs it. Intimacy even helps his health; some men live in such turmoil in the house that it tears them down physically. The two need each other.

But more important is the beauty of her spirit, so you can grow old with her. If you look only at her body and face, when age changes those features and the new car smell wears off, you have nothing left. You never proved the spirit, and you end up hating her because the lust is gone. Marry not for lust but uprightly, that you may be aged and grow together. And sisters, if all you want from a man is his money or physical benefits, when trouble comes and the money goes you end up hating him. Try the spirit by the spirit, and the spirit to try each other by is the Bible. Proving with no Bible open is headed for disaster.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair”: it is not saying a woman can’t have outward adorning. Some think a woman has to look bummy and can never get dressed up. Sisters can plait their hair and get fixed up, “and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel”, but their glory must not be in that. A woman can be all hooked up and her spirit rotten.

“But let it be the hidden man of the heart”: Christ in her spirit. When you find a woman like that, you will have paradise in your marriage.

“In that which is not corruptible”: beauty is corruptible, clothes are corruptible, and they fade. A righteous spirit stays with you, and that is how you grow old in righteousness together, watching the grandkids.

“Even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit”: an ornament is something you see. You see the ornament of her beauty in her wisdom and in how she deals with her brothers and sisters, along with the outward things; but what makes her most beautiful is what doesn’t fade over time. Meek means obedience. Quiet: she is not always screaming, arguing and fighting, ratchet, when the man has just come in from dealing with all that in the street. Why fight the one who keeps a roof over your head and heat in the house? That is biting the hand that feeds you.

“Which is in the sight of God of great price”: that righteous spirit is of great price, a price far beyond rubies. Keep your physical self up as much as you can, because age will get us both, but the inner self is what matters, and believe it or not, the inner spirit makes the outside look good.

“The holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands”: what kind of clothes is that? Verse 3 said not to take your glory from outward adorning; here the holy women adorned themselves with being in subjection to their husbands. That is of great price. That is what you kill for.

“Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord”: that was the adornment Sarah wore. There are jokes about wives saying my lord this and my lord that on the phone with the sisters and cursing him when the phone hangs up; brothers, fix that. His rib, her lord: he is her head, she understands it, and she wakes up the next day and says amen with him. That is where the beauty is.

“Whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well”: daughters of Sarah, as long as you do what we just read. “And are not afraid with any amazement”: trials and things trying to turn you against your husband, things on the job, old dudes looking you up on Facebook and in your DMs wanting to hook up. Don’t even entertain it; block it. Don’t open that door.

“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”: that is why Satan went to her, because she is the weaker vessel. Brothers have to step in so she is not corrupted; your job is to protect her and be a hedge over her. But she has to come in with a basis you can work with, because marriage itself is a trial. Proving can only go so far when you are not living together, and that is no reason to live together in sin. The foundation is that both believe the scriptures. Then the squabbles are small things, how the towels hang. When trouble comes, the question is which one is keeping the commandments: the Bible is what God put together, so one says, the Bible says this, and the other says, you’re right, I was wrong. That is how you keep the peace. If one believes the Bible and the other doesn’t, you are headed for prison, for disaster. That is why the proving process needs heavy emphasis; it is the nucleus of the whole nation of Israel.

“And as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered”: do you wonder why things don’t go right in families? One is trying to keep the commandments and the other is not, and the Lord is not hearing those prayers. If there is evil in your house on any level, the Lord will not bless it. If you are married to someone in the world, hope to convert them, because at some point you will have to part; I can’t move in the righteousness of the Lord if you won’t get yourself together.

This is what you end up with if you don’t prove: women online saying they hate their husbands and wait for him to cheat so they can leave and look like the victim, withholding from him until he cracks. She caused it by treating the man like garbage. And sisters, make sure you don’t get caught up with the wrong brothers who will do you in.

“Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous”: have pity on one another. Even in a marriage you have to love as brethren. Some men are living with a brother sitting in his driveway with a warm can of beer, scared to go into his own house.

precepts.why:
“Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement”: this is the kind of wife you want, the kind of marriage you want: no prison wife, no prison marriage, but paradise, because husband and wife is the nucleus of everything; that is why God set it up that way. “If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.”

Ponder that. A brother whose house is not in order hears it and melts, because he doesn’t have that. People read it and ask, Do women like this even exist? Where is she?

It shows how rare this spirit is: most men do not have a woman who is kind and meek and whose tongue is comforting, and the one who does is not like other men. Since we messed up from the very beginning, women kind, meek and comforting in their speech are rare. Ask a woman and she can name twenty things she doesn’t like about her husband, then has to rack her brain for one or two good ones.

That is what it means to be daughters of Sarah, obeying and calling him lord, as long as you do well: a wife like that is a rarity, and the husband who has her is not like other men.
